text:
Maya Patel: quick idea — propose a "half-life" safety gate for rollforwards of quantized/onboarded model variants. low cost, noise-aware, and avoids hard binary flips.
Noah Kim: sketch? :thinking_face:
Maya Patel: long story short: weight recent traffic/errors with exponential decay (half-life H), require minimum N effective samples and a sustained delta above threshold for T window before traffic increase; immediate fallback if critical alerts spike.
Ravi Gupta: what metrics are we gating on? accuracy delta? hallucination rate? latency regressions?
Maya Patel: primary: eval task accuracy (AUC/EM), user-facing regression signal (ctr/acceptance), and hallucination rate measured by our hallucination-detector eval. secondary: p50/p95 latency, token cost.
Elinor Shaw: need to be careful about small sample variance. how do we choose N and H?
Maya Patel: propose defaults: H = 6 hours, min_effective_samples = 200 (weighted), sustained_delta_margin = 0.8% absolute (or 5% relative), fallback if hallucination_rate increases by >=0.5pp absolute or latency p95 worsens >150ms.
Alex Cho: can we express that in rollout config so infra can enforce auto-fallback? something like:
```
rollout_policy:
  type: half_life_gate
  half_life_hours: 6
  min_effective_samples: 200
  sustained_window_minutes: 60
  delta_margin_absolute: 0.008
  fallback_triggers:
    hallucination_absolute_pp: 0.005
    latency_p95_ms: 150
    critical_errors_rate: 0.01
```
Noah Kim: i like it. also add a statistical check — require that the observed delta exceeds noise_estimate * 1.5 (or p < 0.1) so we don't chase spurious blips.
Ravi Gupta: agree. for noise_estimate we can use bootstrap on rolling baseline slices or use clopper–pearson on binary metrics.
Elinor Shaw: how does half-life avoid being too slow to react to catastrophes?
Maya Patel: immediate fallback triggers (hallucination spike, critical_errors_rate) are instantaneous; half-life is only for gradual promotion/adaptive increases. Also add a floor: if sustained negative delta > 2% for any 15-min window, cut traffic to zero.
Samir: need runbook + dashboards. who owns alerts? postmortem steps?
Maya Patel: proposal: eng-ml owns gate config in model manifest; eng-oncall owns alert routing; runbook in /docs/rollouts/half-life-gate.md (I'll create). Alerts: slack @eng-oncall + pager for critical_errors_rate.
Alex Cho: implement small simulator in staging to validate config before live rollout. can do a 24h shadow run with synthetic drift.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: half-life-gate-v1 -> staging at 2026-03-24T02:00Z
Noah Kim: also document how this interacts with canary: half-life gate should apply once canary passes smoke and we increment traffic fractions. it governs ramp speed beyond initial canary.
Ravi Gupta: one more thought: use per-slice half-life where heavy-signal slices have shorter H to promote faster or revert quicker for critical cohorts.
Elinor Shaw: agree. add config like `slice_overrides: {"mobile": {half_life_hours:2}}`
Maya Patel: next steps: (1) I’ll add PR with YAML schema + runbook draft. (2) Alex to build staging simulator. (3) Ops to wire alerts. (4) we'll do a rehearsal on next canary.
Samir: +1. please tag me for runbook draft review.
Maya Patel: thanks everyone — will open PR today. ping if you want to test heuristics on existing AB traces.
